3. Mr. M Shamsul Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State, submits that as yet 10 his knowledge there is no case against the petitioner and he has got no information about any such case. He concedes that anticipatory bail may be given under section 498 CrPC but he contends that the petitioner does not deserve such a bail. In support of his contention he referred to the case of Sh. Zahoor Ahmed Vs. The State reported in PLD (1974 Lahore) at page 256. In that case it was held as follows: 

 (d) that it should be otherwise a fit case on merits for exercise of discretion in favour of the petitioner for the purpose of bail. In this behalf the provision contained in section 497, CrPC would have to be kept in mind. 

 4. Mr. M Shamsul Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, concedes that all the conditions in this case are fulfilled except the last one, that is, the petitioner did not move any application before the Sessions Judge for anticipatory bail. 

 7. Mr. Khandker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that in a similar case their Lordships of the Appellate Division granted anticipatory bail to the petitioner Golam Sarwar Kamal of that case as reported in BLD Vol. 5 page 110. We have gone through the facts of the above case. The facts of the above case are similar to the facts of the present case. 

 8. We are of opinion that the principle of law laid down in that case is applicable in the facts of the present case. 

 9. Mr. Khandker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner referred to an order of anticipatory bail passed by another Bench of this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 34 of 1991 on 21.1.91. 

 10. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and the legal position discussed above, the prayer for anticipatory bail is allowed for a period of one (1) month from date.
